subject: Information Theory
title: Mesh Networks
description: A quick, practical guide to Mesh Networks.

hook.text: During Hong Kong's 2014 protests, activists used Bridgefy to communicate peer-to-peer when cell towers were overwhelmed.

buildup.text: Mesh networks: every device is both user and router. Messages hop from phone to phone without central infrastructure.

discovery.text: No cell towers, no ISP, no single point of failure. The network exists as long as devices are in range of each other.

twist.text: Mesh networks trade throughput for resilience. Hop-by-hop routing adds latency. Each hop reduces available bandwidth.

climax.text: In disaster zones, mesh networks can restore communication when all infrastructure is destroyed.

punchline.text: Every device a router. No towers needed. The people are the network.

quiz.question: What makes mesh networks resilient?
options: No central infrastructure—every device routes for others
